To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the memory precision for auditory durations is affected by set size, serial position, irrelevant variation, and expectation; and (2) the benefit of having just one item to remember, as opposed to two or more, is vulnerable to the presence of irrelevant variation, and to expectation.

(1) the memory for auditory durations is subject to set-size and serial-position effects; (2) the benefits of a single item in working memory are attenuated by irrelevant information; and (3) the benefits of having only one to-be-remembered item in working memory is stronger when more items were unexpectedly present.

1) memory for sequences of brief time intervals shows set-size and serial-position effects, 2) when irrelevant features are present in the task, memory for a solitary item is worse than for sequences with more than one item, and 3) when irrelevant features were absent, solitary items were recalled more precisely than sequences with more than 1 item, but only when the sequence was unexpectedly short.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way in which information is held in working-memory and how it is prioritized, and how this prioritization is disrupted by attentional demands or expectation.
the way in which we hold brief durations in mind.
the question of whether a sequence of temporal durations is held in working and long-term memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
working memory for sequences of auditory durations is a complex and dynamic process.

the working memory for auditory time durations shows set-size and serial-position effects similar to those observed with other modalities, and these are modulated by the presence of irrelevant features and by expectations.
auditory working memory for temporal intervals is a fragile system that relies heavily on attention and expectations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single-item memory store is more fragile than the memory of multiple items, and that the privileged status of a single item is vulnerable to attentional and expectation effects.
the single-item advantage is not due to a privileged state, but rather to the absence of interference from other items in the memory set.
working memory for sequences of temporal intervals shows a serial position effect and is vulnerable to attentional interference.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mechanisms of working memory for temporal durations are not qualitatively different from those of other modalities, and that the privileged state of one item is vulnerable to disruption by irrelevant information and by expectation.
the memory system is flexible, and that memory for temporal durations can be manipulated by expectations and attentional filtering demands.
working memory for temporal durations is not a single homogeneous system.
